figures.caption: Figure 5. Latency-accuracy curves for SToRe3D under varying sparsity, compared to alternatives. Each point corresponds to a different keep ratio. Increasing sparsity moves models toward higher FPS with only modest drops in mAP.

Figure 1. SToRe3D routes computation via relevance: tokens and queries above stage-wise thresholds are processed further, while the rest are stored for reactivation. The BEV plots and camera images show how queries are reduced across stages based on their relevance scores.

Table 2. Detection performance on nuScenes and nuScenes-R validation set against SOTA methods. Methods are grouped based on comparable latency. Backbone ×W and -S are the image width and sparsity level, respectively. StreamPETR [52], ToC3D [61], SparseBEV [31], Sparse4Dv2 [30], SOLOFusion [41], BEVFormer [27], and Sparse4D [30] are as reported.

Figure 9. Additional qualitative examples of false negatives for the baseline StreamPETR-R50 (left in each pair), where SToRe3D-1/10-ViT-B at a similar latency (right in each pair) correctly detects the planning-critical objects.
Figure 8. Cumulative distribution of closest ego–agent distances on nuScenes, used to select the relevance buffer for our nuScenes-R benchmark.

Figure 7. Latency sensitivity of the ViT backbone and the detection decoder when varying the number of image tokens and object queries independently. The backbone is almost entirely driven by the number of image tokens, while the decoder is much more sensitive to the number of object queries.
Figure 6. Visualization of false negatives for the baseline StreamPETR-R50 (top) and SToRe3D-1/10-ViT-B at similar latency (bottom).
Table 3. Ablation of sparsity approaches [43, 52, 61] at matched total keep ratios (TKR).

Figure 2. SToRe3D architecture builds on a ViT backbone and DETR3D-style decoder with relevance heads that score image tokens and 3D queries at each stage, enabling joint sparsity across backbone and decoder.
Table 5. Model configuration and training hyperparameters used in all experiments.

Table 6. Token pruning schedules for SToRe3D model variants and ToC3D [61]. TKR is the total keep ratio, MKR is the mean keep ratio across layers, and LKRℓ is the layer keep ratio at selected global-attention layers.
Figure 4. Relevant object labeling example geometry.

Figure 3. Planner performance vs. retained agents using a fixed pretrained motion-planning network for analysis only. Planning performance saturates with a subset of agents, motivating relevancebased compute allocation.
